label: Leave one season out

headline.note: An error measure averaged over every region and crop season, as in the viewer. It is not a total; the per-region figures are below.

headline_note: In both tests the model is given the actual weather of the season it predicts. So this shows how well it turns weather into yield, not how well anyone can forecast next year's weather.
caveat: Model settings were tuned on these same seasons, and the tests use farm averages rather than single fields, so real-world errors are likely to be larger.

methods.label: Baseline: farm average
methods.text: The farm's average yield for that crop across the training seasons. It knows the farm but ignores weather, so it predicts about the same number every season.

methods.label: Our model: weather-aware regression
methods.text: Farm effect + technology trend + soil + irrigation + crop-stage weather (drought, heat, rain at sowing and harvest). It uses no same-season farm inputs, because those aren't known in advance.

by_crop_note: Average gap between predicted and actual total production per season. Shorter is better.
pea_models_note: Peas from both regions share one model. Long-range results use one weather response for both regions, because 9 Swedish seasons can't support a separate one. The 2027–2031 forecast keeps separate responses.

scorer.note: Apetit told us this score doesn't affect their decision. On this test, the official formula gives our model 71.1 and the baseline 38.1. It's applied to farm-level rows while the hidden answers are per field, so expect the real score to be lower.

c1_self_check.note: Live predictions against the submitted C1 file on a sample of 60 rows (the file is rounded to 3 decimals).
